newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq says 800,000 children died due to sanctions.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says 800,000 children died due to sanctions.

text.p: More than 800,000 children have died as a result of medical shortages during nearly seven years of U.N. trade sanctions, an official said on Thursday.

Head of the Iraqi Society for Children's Support, Sultan al-Shawi, said the most vulnerable group was children under five years more than 300,000 of whom had died since the sanctions were imposed on Iraq for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
"The unjust embargo on Iraq has caused the death of 839,400 children from August 1990 until April 1997," al-Shawi said at a news conference attended by foreign reporters in Baghdad.

The sanctions do not bar Iraq from importing medicine and food but Baghdad has little cash to pay for them. Under a deal with the United Nations launched in December, Iraq is selling oil worth $2 billion over six months to buy urgent needs.
The first shipment of medical supplies bought under the pact reached Iraq last week.
Figures published by the Iraqi Health Ministry indicated that about 30,000 Iraqis died each year before the sanctions, compared to 140,000 now.
Shawi cited malnutrition and diarrhoea among the main causes of the rising mortality rate among children.
